card.keepWhy: You can say anything to God. Even “how long?”

check: The lesson places Psalm 13 in David’s years on the run as a way of telling it; Psalm 13 itself names no event (Psalms 57 and 142 do). Confirm this framing is acceptable.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever been angry at God, or felt you weren’t allowed to be?
options: thank you for saying it. you’re not alone, and this story proves it.
listen to this one. the bible itself might surprise you.
good. keep this for a day you might need it.

steps.line: Young David played music for King Saul. But as David became loved by the people, Saul grew jealous, and turned against him.
steps.label: 1 Samuel 18

steps.line: David ran for his life. For years he lived in the wilderness, hiding in caves, with the king’s soldiers on his trail.
steps.label: 1 Samuel 23-24

steps.line: The Bible keeps a book of songs, many linked to David, called psalms. Some were sung in the darkest times.

steps.q: Hunted, hiding, far from home. Some of these songs are angry with God. How do you guess most of them end?
o: Turning back to trust in God
With a curse on the enemy
steps.why: Most laments turn to trust before they end, often with a promise to praise. Not all: Psalm 88 ends in darkness, and it was kept in the Bible too.
“Forget.” The psalm says out loud what it feels like: that God has forgotten.

steps.line: “How long, Lord? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?”
steps.label: Psalm 13:1

steps.q: Why do you think songs this angry were kept in the Bible, and are still prayed today?
o: They were too old and loved to leave out
Complaint spoken to God is itself a prayer
Their happy endings made them acceptable
steps.why: It’s called lament, and laments are the largest single group among the psalms, about a third of them.

steps.line: But the same short psalm ends, “I will sing to the Lord, because he has been good to me.”
steps.label: Psalm 13:6

steps.q: The angry psalms had one more famous voice. Where did Jesus pray one out loud?
o: At his baptism, in the river
At the wedding feast in Cana
On the cross, as he was dying
steps.why: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” is the first line of Psalm 22, a lament that also ends in praise.

say: here’s what i love. the bible doesn’t just allow anger at God. it hands you the words.
jews and christians have prayed the psalms for centuries, the angry ones too. you only shout at someone you believe is listening.

steps.q: The psalm ends in a song, but nothing in the danger has changed yet. So what changed?
o: He decided he’d been wrong to complain
Saying it all brought him back to trust
He chose to sound grateful anyway
steps.why: He said everything, and was still talking to God at the end. Honesty kept the door open.

today.say: if something’s been eating at you, tell God straight today, out loud or on paper: “how long?” then end, as david did, with one thing that’s still good. pray it, write it, or just read psalm 13 slowly: your choice.
options: then say it. all of it. he can take it.
good. let david’s words say it for you for now.
